title: Kotor Serpentine & Lovćen: 25 Hairpins Above the Boka
subRegion: Bay of Kotor, Lovćen NP & the Old Royal Capital

bestPeriod.avoid: July-August, 35 °C at sea level, cruise-ship coach convoys on the bay road, and the serpentine's daytime one-way restrictions at their tightest; December-February brings snow and ice above 1,000 m on Lovćen.

accommodation.note: Kotor/Dobrota guesthouse €55, €95 pppn; one night in Njeguši or Cetinje €40, €60

food.note: Konoba mains €9, €16; Njeguši pršut-and-cheese board €12; coastal fish is double

transport.note: Airport transfer, Kamenari-Lepetane ferry, one cable-car lift, van recovery

activities.note: Road bike hire €180, €240/week, Lovćen NP entry, Mausoleum, Cetinje museums

profile.difficultyNote: 4/5, five riding days between 800 m and 1,900 m of ascent, with one climb that gains nearly a kilometre of altitude in a single unbroken hour

gatewayAirport: TIV Tivat, 25 min drive / 22 km ride to Kotor; PDG Podgorica 1 h 30 min; DBV Dubrovnik 2 h with a land border that can add 90 min in summer
summary: This is a week built around one road. The old Austro-Hungarian carriage road from Kotor to Njeguši, the P1, the Kotor Serpentine, the Ladder of Cattaro's tarmac successor, stacks twenty-five numbered hairpins into a limestone wall and lifts you from the quay to a saddle at nearly 950 m without a single flat metre. Everything else in the week is arranged around that climb: a bay warm-up on the Perast-Risan shore, the high plateau of Lovćen NP and Njegoš's mausoleum, the imperial small-town calm of Cetinje, a gravel day into the Krivošije backcountry, a Vrmac ridge traverse, and a coastal spin down the Budva riviera. It suits climbers who are comfortable descending on narrow roads with hip-height stone parapets and, sometimes, none.

itinerary.title: Land at Tivat, ride the bay to Kotor
itinerary.morning: Collect the bike in Tivat or ride the 22 km shore road from the airport around the bay through Prčanj and Muo, with the walls of Kotor opening ahead. Traffic is heavy but slow.
itinerary.afternoon: Settle in Dobrota, then a flat spin north along the waterfront promenade to Ljuta and back, 16 km with almost no ascent, purely to check cleats, brakes and gearing before anything serious.
itinerary.evening: Konoba Ćatovića Mlini at Morinj, a restored watermill on the bay north of Kotor, for grilled fish and the house bread. Book a day ahead.
itinerary.dayStats: 38 km / 210 m ascent / 100% paved / airport-to-Kotor 22 km

itinerary.title: Perast, Risan and the Roman mosaics
itinerary.morning: North on the bay road to **Perast**, park the bike at the quay and take the shuttle boat to **Our Lady of the Rocks**, the artificial islet built on centuries of dropped stones. Climb the bell tower of St Nicholas for the strait view.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue to **Risan** for the 2nd-century Roman villa mosaics, including the sleeping Hypnos, then loop back with the short climb to **Kostanjica**. Save the legs.
itinerary.evening: Back in Kotor, eat at Konoba Portun in the Old Town, black risotto and buzara. Walk the Sea Gate and the Square of Arms afterwards.
itinerary.dayStats: 46 km / 480 m ascent / 96% paved / Our Lady of the Rocks boat ≈€5 return

itinerary.title: The Serpentine: twenty-five hairpins to Njeguši
itinerary.morning: Leave Dobrota by 07:00. The climb starts at the Škaljari roundabout; hairpin 1 is signed within two kilometres. The gradient sits at 5-7% and never relents, pace it as an hour of steady tempo, not an effort. Fort Gorazda and the Ladder of Cattaro mule path cross the road twice.
itinerary.afternoon: Over the **Krstac saddle at 940 m** and down the far side into **Njeguši**, the Petrović dynasty's home village, for pršut air-dried in the mountain draught and Njeguški sir. Descend the serpentine mid-afternoon.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at Galion, on the water below the walls, watching the light leave the cliff you climbed.
itinerary.dayStats: 44 km / 1,150 m ascent / 100% paved / P1 climb 16 km at 5.8%, max 11%, 25 hairpins

itinerary.title: Lovćen, the Mausoleum and down to Cetinje
itinerary.morning: The serpentine again, but this time through Njeguši and on into **Lovćen National Park**, climbing gently across karst pasture and black-pine forest to **Ivanova Korita (1,270 m)**.
itinerary.afternoon: The spur to the **Njegoš Mausoleum** car park at ≈1,570 m, then 461 steps on foot through the rock tunnel to Jezerski vrh (1,657 m), Meštrović's granite Njegoš under a gold mosaic vault, and a view that on a clear day reaches the Albanian Alps. Long descent to **Cetinje (671 m)**.
itinerary.evening: Cetinje is a former royal capital of embassy villas and closed shutters. Eat at Kole for cicvara and priganice; the town is quiet by 22:00 and that is the point.
itinerary.dayStats: 62 km / 1,900 m ascent / 100% paved / high point 1,570 m ridden, 1,657 m walked / 461 steps

itinerary.title: Vrmac ridge and the Kamenari ferry
itinerary.morning: Roll the fast 30 km descent from Cetinje to Budva, then the coast to Tivat. Alternatively shuttle back to Kotor and start fresh.
itinerary.afternoon: Climb from Škaljari to **Trojica** and onto the **Vrmac military road**, graded limestone gravel along the whole ridge to **Fort Vrmac (785 m)**, an intact Austro-Hungarian work with the bay on one side and Tivat on the other. Descend to Gornja Lastva and Tivat, ride to Lepetane, take the **ferry to Kamenari**, and return along the north shore.
itinerary.evening: Konoba Feral in Herceg Novi if you extend, or back in Dobrota for grilled squid.
itinerary.dayStats: 58 km / 1,050 m ascent / 70% paved, 30% gravel / Vrmac climb 9.5 km at 7.9% / ferry €1 with a bike, 10 min

itinerary.title: Krivošije backcountry gravel
itinerary.morning: North to **Risan**, then up the Grahovo road's own serpentines into the **Krivošije**, a limestone plateau of sinkholes, abandoned Austro-Hungarian blockhouses and villages of four people. Traffic effectively stops after the first ten hairpins.
itinerary.afternoon: Gravel spurs around **Dragalj** and the Han Dragalj junction, then the open road to **Grahovo** if legs allow. Carry all your food and 2 litres of water, there is no shop between Risan and Grahovo you can rely on.
itinerary.evening: Return by the same descent, which is the finest unphotographed descent in Montenegro. Dinner at Konoba Akustik, Dobrota.
itinerary.dayStats: 74 km / 1,450 m ascent / 65% paved, 35% gravel / Risan climb 19 km at 4.6% / high point ≈900 m

itinerary.title: Budva riviera and out
itinerary.morning: Over the low Trojica pass to Budva and along the riviera to Sveti Stefan, Pržno and Rijeka Reževići, rolling, 4-8% pitches, sea on your left the whole way.
itinerary.afternoon: Turn at Petrovac, ride back to Tivat, wash and return the bike. Swim at Jaz if the water is warm enough.
itinerary.evening: Late flight from TIV, or a last dinner in Kotor's Old Town at Bastion.
itinerary.dayStats: 68 km / 900 m ascent / 100% paved / Kotor-Budva 22 km, Budva-Petrovac 18 km
itinerary.sleep: Airport-side Tivat room, or out on the evening flight

accommodationStrategy.name: Dobrota waterfront guesthouse
accommodationStrategy.description: The functional base for the whole week: ground-floor or courtyard bike storage, a tap and hose for salt and limestone dust, parking if you also have a car, and a flat 2 km promenade into the Old Town so you never carry a bike up steps. Roughly €55, €95 per room per night in shoulder season.

accommodationStrategy.name: A Njeguši village house
accommodationStrategy.description: Sleeping at the top of the serpentine flips the week: you descend to breakfast and climb home. Rooms are simple, heating matters even in May, and dinner is whatever the household is smoking. Around €40, €60 per room, cash. Worth one night to ride Lovćen on fresh legs.

accommodationStrategy.name: Small guesthouse, central Cetinje
accommodationStrategy.description: The right overnight for the Lovćen point-to-point, saving a 900 m re-climb at the end of the hardest day. Bikes go in a hallway or shed; ask explicitly. Cetinje is 40 minutes' descent from the coast and 10 °C cooler in June.

logistics.connectivity: 4G is strong through the bay, along the coast and in Cetinje; it thins on the Lovćen plateau and is genuinely absent in parts of the Krivošije around Dragalj. **Montenegro is outside EU roaming**, though EU-operator rates to the Western Balkans have been reduced by agreement, check your tariff or buy a local prepaid SIM (Telekom, One, m:tel) at Tivat airport for a few euro. Download offline maps for the whole Boka.
logistics.emergency: 112 works nationally; ambulance 124, police 122. Mountain rescue is coordinated through 112 and is thin on Lovćen, response to the plateau can take well over an hour. The nearest full hospital is Kotor General; serious trauma goes to Podgorica. **Montenegro is not in the EU and EHIC/GHIC do not apply**, carry travel insurance that names road cycling and repatriation.
logistics.weather: The bay is one of the wettest places in Europe, Crkvice, above Risan, records some of the continent's highest annual rainfall. Expect violent, short autumn downpours that make the serpentine's polished tarmac treacherous. The **bura** funnels down the mountain wall in winter and shoulder season and can gust hard at Krstac. Temperature drops 8-12 °C between Kotor quay and the Mausoleum: always carry a packable jacket and long fingers.
logistics.bookingWindows: Bay accommodation for June and September should be booked 6-10 weeks ahead; July-August, four months. Bikes at Bajković or 3E: 3-4 weeks in shoulder season. Ćatovića Mlini: a day or two. Nothing on Lovćen needs booking except a Njeguši room, which needs a phone call.
logistics.money: Montenegro uses the **euro unilaterally** without being in the eurozone or the EU. Cards are accepted in Kotor, Budva and Tivat; Njeguši households, mountain konobas, the Krivošije and small ferries are cash. Carry €50, €80 in small notes. Tipping is rounding up, 10% for a proper dinner.
logistics.transportRules: No road vignette in Montenegro; the Sozina tunnel toll (≈€3.50 for cars) is irrelevant here. **Bicycles are banned from Sozina and are a bad idea in the Vrmac road tunnel**, take the ridge or the ferry instead. Rental cars crossing to Croatia, Bosnia or Albania need a green card and written permission from the rental firm; expect a €30, €60 cross-border fee. The Kamenari-Lepetane ferry needs no booking.
logistics.permits: **Lovćen National Park** charges a modest per-person entry (a few euro) at the Ivanova Korita gate; the **Njegoš Mausoleum** is a separate ticket of roughly €5. Cyclists are frequently waved through the park gate but should carry cash. Drones require Civil Aviation Agency approval and are prohibited over the Mausoleum and the Kotor fortifications, which are UNESCO-listed. Wild camping in the national park is not permitted.
logistics.health: Tap water in Kotor, Cetinje and Njeguši is potable; assume nothing in the Krivošije. Ticks are present in Lovćen's pasture and forest edge April-October. The single biggest hazard is **descending traffic on the serpentine**, tour vans, hire cars on the wrong line, and drivers stopped mid-hairpin for photographs. Descend on the outside of your lane, cover the brakes, and use a loud rear light in the tunnels.

proTips: **Ride the serpentine uphill before 08:00 and downhill before 10:00.** In the summer season the P1 operates directional restrictions, descending traffic is barred through the middle of the day and ascending traffic in the late afternoon, precisely to stop the road gridlocking. Cyclists are not the target, but you do not want to be in the queue that results. Check the signs at the Škaljari roundabout on arrival.

**Count the hairpins.** They are numbered on small posts; if you lose count you have miscounted, because there are exactly 25 on the Kotor side. It is a genuinely useful pacing tool, a third of the climb is done by number 9.

**Use the Kotor Cable Car as a one-way lift** if you want the Lovćen plateau without the climb, or to salvage a day of bad legs. Bikes go in the gondolas for a supplement; it shuts in strong wind, so it is not a plan you can rely on.

**Buy pršut in Njeguši at a house, not a restaurant.** The village smokehouses sell whole and sliced; the mountain draught and the sea air are the entire point of the product and it is half the coastal price.
**Do the Krivošije day with 35 mm+ tyres and full food.** Between Risan and Grahovo you will pass more abandoned blockhouses than open shops. There is no water tap you can count on after Risan.

**Skip the Vrmac road tunnel on a bike.** It is unlit, has no walkway and carries fast traffic. The ridge gravel is the whole reason to be on Vrmac anyway, and the Lepetane ferry gets you home for a euro.
**Base in Dobrota, not inside the walls.** Kotor's Old Town is stairs, alleys and cruise-ship crowds from 09:00, and getting a bike in or out of it is a daily argument.
**Take a rear light for the serpentine even in daylight.** The short rock galleries near the top are unlit and drivers coming down out of the sun genuinely will not see you.
**Ride Lovćen on a Tuesday or Wednesday.** Cetinje and the Mausoleum absorb the coastal coach tours at weekends, and the plateau road is single-lane in places.

raw.Loop 1, The Serpentine and Njeguši (Days: Kotor → P1 serpentine → Krstac saddle → Njeguši → back down. **44 km / 1,150 m ascent.** The out-and-back is the classic; the descent is the reason people come.
raw.Loop 2, Lovćen crown (Day 4): Kotor → serpentine → Njeguši → Ivanova Korita → Njegoš Mausoleum car park → Cetinje. **62 km / 1,900 m ascent**, point-to-point, ending in Cetinje.
raw.Loop 3, Vrmac ridge (Day 5): Kotor → Škaljari → Trojica → Vrmac military road → Fort Vrmac → Gornja Lastva → Tivat → Lepetane ferry → Kamenari → Kotor. **58 km / 1,050 m ascent.**
raw.Loop 4, Krivošije gravel (Day 6): Risan → Krivošije serpentines → Dragalj → Grahovo → return. **74 km / 1,450 m ascent.**
raw.Kotor Serpentine (P1), Kotor → Krstac sa: ≈16 km, 930 m gained, **5.8% average**, ramps to **11%** on hairpins 18-24, summit **940 m**. Twenty-five numbered switchbacks, all paved, carriageway 3.5-5 m with passing bays. Roughly 300 m of unlit short tunnels/rock galleries near the top, carry a rear light.
raw.Krstac → Njeguši → Ivanova Korita: a further 18 km at **3-6%**, topping 1,270 m at Ivanova Korita, then the spur to the **Mausoleum car park at ≈1,570 m**, the last 4 km hold **7-9%**.
raw.Krivošije from Risan (toward Grahovo): ≈19 km, 880 m, **4.6% average**, max 9%, its own set of Austro-Hungarian hairpins and about a third the traffic of the Kotor side.
raw.Vrmac from Škaljari to Fort Vrmac: 9.5 km, 760 m, **7.9% average**, max 14% on the concrete ramps above Trojica; summit fort **785 m**.
raw.Week surface split: ≈78% paved (narrow, chip-sealed, no shoulder), 16% graded limestone gravel on the Vrmac military road and Krivošije spurs, 4% rough double-track around Dragalj, 2% cobbled village lane in Njeguši. A 28-32 mm tyre covers the road days; take 35-40 mm if you want the Krivošije and Vrmac days properly.
raw.Bike hire: **Bajković Bike** (bajkovicbike.com) rents from Kotor and Dobrota, city, trekking, MTB and e-bikes, roughly **€15, €25/day** for a hybrid and **€35, €45/day** e-bike, with weekly rates around €90, €180. **3E Travel** (3etravel.me) rents in both Kotor and Podgorica, which makes a Kotor-pick-up/Podgorica-drop feasible for a one-way finish, expect a **€30, €60 relocation charge**. **Montenegro Plus** (montenegroplus.me) supplies e-MTB and trekking fleets for bay tours. Genuine carbon road bikes with compact gearing are scarce: if you want 34×34 or lower for the Mausoleum spur, bring your own bike or reserve months ahead.
raw.Bike-friendly accommodation logistics: Nowhere in Kotor's walled Old Town has step-free bike access, it is all stairs and alleys, and the town gates close to vehicles. Sleep in **Dobrota**, along the waterfront north of the walls, where guesthouses have ground-floor rooms, gated courtyards and a hose. Confirm a locked indoor space in writing; cycle theft in the bay is real. Njeguši and Cetinje properties are simple houses with a shed or a hallway.
raw.Bikes on ferries and buses: The **Kamenari-Lepetane ferry** across the Verige strait runs 24 hours, every 15-20 minutes by day, crossing in about 10 minutes. A car is roughly **€5**; foot passengers cross free and **a bicycle is €1 or waved through**. No booking, no timetable to plan around, just ride on. Intercity buses (Blue Line, Autoboka) take a bike in the luggage bay for **€1, €2 at the driver's discretion**, wheel out, and refuse point-blank when the bay is full. There is no train in the Boka. The **Kotor Cable Car** (Dub, above Kotor, to Kuk at ≈1,350 m on the Lovćen plateau) carries bikes in the gondolas for a supplement and turns the serpentine into a descent-only day, around **€25 return, €17 one-way**, closed in high wind.
